newsitem.title: USA: US FCC chief appeals to Asia to open telecom markets.
newsitem.headline: US FCC chief appeals to Asia to open telecom markets.

text.p: The nation's top communications regulator Friday appealed to Asian nations to open their telecommunications markets during the ongoing talks over telecommunications trade at the World Trade Organization.

"A principal purpose of my trip to Hong Kong is to urge Asian countries to improve their offers in the WTO telecom talks that are scheduled to end next February," Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said in a speech to the Asia Society in Hong Kong. A transcript was released in Washington.
"If these talks are to succeed, Asian countries must make better offers."

Hundt also directed his comments at Hong Kong regulators. He said the island's state-run phone monopoly "causes consumers in both the United States and Hong Kong to pay a very fishy price -- a price for international service between Hong Kong and the United States that is many times above the cost of such service."

Hundt said the ability of Hong Kong Telecom "to extract monopoly rents from consumers in the U.S. and Hong Kong is not consistent with the principles of competition and open markets for which Hong Kong is so justly famous."
